subject: Timebound egress addendum, KMS evidence & subprocessor deactivation plan
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@finhealth.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@finhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot request — temporary cross-region processing + DPA addendum

Hi Priyom / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a narrowly scoped pilot starting next Monday and have one operational/legal ask before we flip the switch: our security policy requires any temporary cross-border processing to be covered by a short addendum to the DPA and a clear operational window. Concretely, we need:

- a 72-hour timebound egress window for EU->US to support a one-off analytics job (window to be scheduled; must be auditable)
- evidence that the data path will use a customer-supplied KMS key or, if not possible, documentation of the KMS separation guarantees and key rollover process
- an updated subprocessor roster that shows any transient cloud partners that may touch the data during the window and a plan to deactivate those subprocessors afterwards
- a DocuSign-ready addendum we can sign this week

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) provide a DPA addendum template that limits the window to a specified UTC range and includes an audit log clause,
2) either support customer-managed keys for the pilot or provide a short-proof-of-control note for your KMS configuration, and
3) supply a subprocessor deactivation checklist we can attach to the signature?

We appreciate quick confirmation — legal needs the paperwork to greenlight the pilot.

Best,
Alex
Alex Carter
Head of Security Programs
FinHealth

--

Hi Alex,

Thanks — we can support a timebound, auditable egress window for pilots. High level answers below; Kimberly & Ops will follow with runbook details and the subprocessor CSV.

1) DPA addendum: legal can prepare a short addendum that explicitly enumerates the UTC start/end times and references tokenized audit logs. I can push a DocuSign packet to the link below once we confirm the scheduled window.
2) KMS: we support customer-managed keys in our Private and Dedicated products. For Hosted pilots we can provide an intermediary proof-of-control package (KMS architecture diagram + key access audit) if a CMK is not provisioned. Please confirm which model you plan to run on (hosted vs. dedicated).
3) Subprocessor deactivation: Ops will provide a one-page checklist and a roster CSV that shows who will be active during the window and steps taken to terminate access afterwards.

Next steps I propose:
- Alex: confirm desired UTC window (suggested: 2028-07-21T02:00:00Z -> 2028-07-24T02:00:00Z)
- Kimberly: attach ops_runbook + roster and confirm whether the pilot will run on Hosted or Dedicated
- Marissa: legal will draft the DPA addendum and route for signature

I’ll keep this thread as the canonical thread for the paperwork.

Thanks,
Priyom Das

On Fri, Jul 14, 2028 at 10:05 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I’ll keep this thread as the canonical thread for the paperwork.

Alex — quick technical confirmation from ops:

- Window: 72-hour window as proposed (2028-07-21T02:00:00Z -> 2028-07-24T02:00:00Z) is feasible. We will implement a strict circuit that limits KV cache replication and disables cross-region telemetry outside the window.
- Hosted vs Dedicated: if you run on Hosted we cannot import your CMK into our multi-tenant KMS, but we can provide the KMS proof-of-control package (audit trail + separation diagram + recent key usage logs). If you need a CMK, Dedicated is the supported path — we can provision a customer-managed key under a Dedicated reservation and attach policies that ensure only the pilot job can access the key for the window.
- Subprocessors: attached is the subprocessor_roster_2028-07.csv (names + roles) and ops_runbook_timebound-egress_v1.pdf (runbook stub). The runbook includes ops checklist items: pre-window snapshot, temporary ACL change, run job, verify audit, revoke ACL, and confirmation note.

Action items for Redwood:
- Ops will coordinate a 24-hour dry run (no data egress) on 2028-07-20 to exercise the checklist.
- Security will compile the KMS proof-of-control packet and upload to the DocuSign bundle.

I’ve attached the files mentioned above. Let me know if you need more granular log samples; we can redact PII and supply tokenized traces for review.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: ops_runbook_timebound-egress_v1.pdf (PDF stub), subprocessor_roster_2028-07.csv (CSV stub)

Thanks — this looks good and aligns with our security requirements. We accept the 72-hour window and the 2028-07-20 dry run. Two quick asks before Marissa routes the addendum: 

1) please attach the KMS proof-of-control packet (redacted logs + diagram) to the DocuSign bundle, and
2) add a one-line clause in the addendum that commits Redwood to a post-window debrief (signed confirmation that subprocessors were deactivated).

If you can get the DocuSign packet ready by Tuesday (2028-07-18 EOD UTC) legal will sign and we’ll schedule the dry run.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
